chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Washa, who said:
I wrote to him, meaning Al-Rida (peace be upon him), asking him about Al-Fuqaa'. He said, so he wrote: 'It is prohibited, and it is wine, and whoever drinks it is in the status of the wine drinker.'
He said, and Abu Al-Hasan the Last (peace be upon him) said: 'If the house were my house, I would have killed its seller and whipped its drinker.'
And Abu Al-Hasan the Last (peace be upon him) said: 'Its legal penalty (Hadd) is the legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a wine which the people have considered trivial.'

key_terms.الْفُقَّاع: Al-Fuqaa, a specific type of fermented drink
key_terms.خُمَيْرَة: A type of wine or fermented drink

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on Al-Fuqaa and how does it compare to wine?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (AS) establishes 'Al-Fuaa' as prohibited by equating it to wine, while Imam Al-Hadi (AS) emphasizes the severity of its consumption by stating he would kill its seller and lash its drinker, confirming its legal penalty (hadd) matches that of wine. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the intoxicating nature of a drink, rather than its specific preparation or name, determines its status as *khamr*, addressing the common underestimation of its potency.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Washa who said,

‘I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the fermented drinks. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘It is prohibited and it is wine, and the one who drinks it would be at the status of the wine drinker’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the Last said: ‘If the house was my<sup>asws</sup> house, I<sup>asws</sup> would have killed its seller, and would have whipped its drinker’.
And Abu Al-Hassanasws the Last said: ‘Its legal penalty (Hadd) is a legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a wine which the people are considering it as trivial’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Washsha’ who has said the following: “
I once wrote to al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about al-Fuqa’. He (the Imam) wrote back, ‘It is unlawful and it is wine. If one drinks it he is like a wine drinker.’
He (the narrator) has said that abu al-Hassan, al-Akhir, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Had the house been my house I would execute its seller and whip its drinker.’
He (the Imam) has also said, ‘The penalty for drinking al-Fuqa ’ is the same as for drinking wine.’
He (the Imam) has said, ‘It is intoxicating liquor which people have taken lightly.’”
